note: IT-6 ran end to end against PayPal Sandbox on 2026-11-03 between 14:05Z and 15:26Z: a real two-lot auction decided from real sealed bids, a buyer approving a real order, a real authorization captured to COMPLETED, that capture refunded to COMPLETED, and a second lot left short of its minimum so its live authorization is voided on the fund deadline. The API and the job worker both ran on loopback against the local compose database with PAYMENT_ROUTER=single_seller, PAYMENT_MODE=authorize_capture, PAYPAL_APPROVAL_UI=redirect and WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=false, so the timers and the reconciler were the only thing moving state -- the alternative IT-6's own text names.
earlier_partial_run: A first run the same day, 13:01Z to 13:18Z, executed the auction half and created three real PayPal orders (5RH40086MG743532T, 8RK07718KJ297035W, 4GW6051813401951B). Its offers expired at 13:44:13Z before any approval, so nothing in it moved money; it is kept as the run that first proved the award fixes in a live server.
pool: Two lots in US-EAST from one template: lot 1 seats 1 minimum 1, lot 2 seats 2 minimum 2. Entry window closed 14:37:48Z, bid window 600 s, offer window and fund deadline both 15:23:48Z.
auction: Three buyers joined through POST /intake/manual and POST /pools/{id}/entries, each taking a signed receipt, and one receipt was read back through the CR-9 route. Two merchants placed four sealed bids through PUT /merchant/lots/{lot_id}/bid, each with its receipt hash, and confirmed them inside the window. lot.award then decided both lots in lot_order: lot 1 AWARDED to the 47000-cent merchant with its rival LOST; on lot 2 the same cheap merchant came back REJECTED with R9_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED -- one of its two declared seats was already spent on lot 1 while its lot-2 bid declared capacity for two -- so lot 2 AWARDED to the 49000-cent merchant. Both lots reached CHECKOUT_OPEN and lot.open_checkout created one offer per seated buyer.
funded_lot: Buyer order a0793957-c8f1-46aa-97f8-207cf086273e on lot 1. PayPal order 73Y52576X51398922, approved by a US Sandbox buyer and confirmed by the server through POST /offers/{id}/approved at 14:55:56Z, which returned APPROVED: every FR-CK-05 check passed against a fresh GET rather than against the redirect. Authorization 1C716592GL014192L, capture 8J691800FS7606033. The capture reads COMPLETED 470.00 USD when GET directly from PayPal, and that authorization reads CAPTURED there. Ledger for the lot: AUTH_CREATED 47000 then CAPTURE_COMPLETED 47000, with one distinct paid buyer against moq 1, so LS-06 took the lot to FUNDING and LS-07 to FUNDED at funded_at 14:56:09.869891Z.
refund: That capture was then refunded through BO-13's ops branch: refund 2AR89715765309632 reads COMPLETED 470.00 USD at PayPal and the capture itself now reads REFUNDED there. The ledger gained REFUND_PENDING 47000 then REFUND_COMPLETED 47000 and the lot's net paid cents is 0 by the ledger service's own formula. The trigger was an ops refund, not a lot failure, and it is labelled as that: the abort route that would fail a lot on command is still a NotImplementedError stub, so a FAILING lot cannot be produced at will, and a lot that has funded has no legitimate way to hold a completed capture and then fail. Whether PayPal keeps its fee on a refund is NOT answered by this run -- the capture's seller_payable_breakdown came back with gross_amount, paypal_fee and net_amount all null in the Sandbox read -- so no fee claim is made either way.
failing_lot: Lot 2 held two seats with a minimum of two and got one approval. Buyer order 3880b683-39df-4c55-a995-d039e705c15b was approved at 14:55:56Z and authorized -- authorization 4M283808TA524902D, 490.00 USD -- while buyer order e3b55344 stayed ORDER_CREATED because its buyer never approved. LS-06's threshold for that lot is min(seats 2, moq 2 + buffer 0) = 2 authorizations, so it stayed CHECKOUT_OPEN and no capture was ever enqueued for it. Its fund deadline was 15:22:49Z, but the lot was still CHECKOUT_OPEN at 15:24; LS-08 applied only at 15:25:10Z, after a lot.try_fund job was enqueued by hand, and LS-10 reached FAILED_CLOSED at 15:25:21Z with the authorization voided (void_source lot_failing) and the untouched offer expired. That gap is written up as Q-2026-11-03-32 rather than glossed over: the deadline pass did not decide the lot at the deadline. Ledger for the lot: AUTH_CREATED 49000 then AUTH_VOIDED 49000, no capture row, net paid cents 0.
webhooks: Five real deliveries from this run reached the deployed listener and were stored by it with their signature headers: two CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED, two PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED and one PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED. The capture event WH-67H061729H899170V-8Y109638XV12376 was harvested from the deployed app's own table and verified -- see webhook_delivery.json.
how_to_run: 1. Export PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET and SINGLE_SELLER_EMAIL for the app-owning FairPool Sandbox app, and set PAYMENT_MODE=authorize_capture, PAYPAL_APPROVAL_UI=redirect, PAYMENT_ROUTER=single_seller, WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=false. DONE.
2. Point DATABASE_URL at a migrated local database (alembic upgrade head, currently 0006) and start the API. DONE -- 127.0.0.1:8010 with the worker beside it.
3. Create one pool with two lots: lot 1 seats 1 minimum 1, lot 2 seats 2 minimum 2, require_paypal_link false. DONE.

4. Two merchants bid through the real path and confirm, so lot.bid_open, lot.bid_close and lot.award decide from real bids and lot.open_checkout opens checkout. No admin force-award. DONE through the structured bid route; the quote-paste route is the Gemini-quota item below.
5. Buyers join through the buyer UI (Discover -> lobby -> join -> receipt). DONE through the routes the UI calls.
6. Drain jobs through the registered handlers. DONE -- the worker ran the whole lifecycle, reconciler sweep included.
7. Each selected buyer opens their own offer and approves on the PayPal Sandbox page. DONE by the owner at 14:55Z for two of the three offers.

8. The sweep authorizes, then captures the approved orders; lot 1 reaches FUNDED when completed captures from distinct buyers meet its minimum. DONE -- FUNDED at 14:56:09Z with one distinct paid buyer.

9. Lot 2 misses its minimum: authorizations are voided, any completed capture is refunded, and the ledger for that lot nets to zero. DONE at the 15:23:48Z deadline; the real refund in this run came from lot 1 through the ops branch and is labelled as that.
10. Record the provider references in this file, with no token, client secret or full approval URL. DONE.
not_claimed: No live vault-charge path (VAULT_REAL_SAVE_ENABLED stays false), no webhook-driven money move (WEBHOOKS_ENABLED is false locally, so the deliveries prove delivery and signature, not processing), and no second-seller routing. The refund-fee question is left open rather than guessed.
needs_from_owner: A Gemini API key with quota for the quote-parsing leg. The free-tier key in .env returns 429 and the quote path refuses with FEATURE_DISABLED rather than pretending to parse, so that leg is stated as not executed.
Rotate or delete IT6_BUYER_PASSWORD in .env: the three Sandbox buyer accounts were used for this run and their password sat in the chat and then in the environment file.
credential_handling: No token, client secret, buyer password, approval URL or raw provider body is recorded here. Provider references only: order, authorization, capture and refund ids, amounts in integer cents, and the ledger kinds beside them. Approval URLs were reached through a loopback redirector so they never entered a log or this file, and the raw webhook body stays in the gitignored .tmp capture file.
fixture_note: The run's admin and merchant accounts are local fixtures made the way tools/demo_seed.py makes its own: IdentityService.register in-process, then the role and the merchant profile with the three R2 attestations. The HTTP register route is the PayPal-first signup path only, so it is not how a fixture account is made. The first bid attempt 403'd because that fixture forgot the merchant role flip.
